\frontchapter{Abstract}
JHQ-GPU studies how to execute JHQ's compressed primary/residual search efficiently within GPU memory. For fixed computed primary scores, grouped retention, merging and witnessed shared bounds preserve global top-$c$ selection under the stated ordering and memory-access conditions. Cartesian splitting replaces 256 LUT entries with $16+16$, giving a storage ratio $32/256=1/8$ with the same real-arithmetic score. Calibration compares sampled top-$k$ IDs with a larger-budget reference, without GT or a learned predictor.

On six RTX 5090 datasets, two-group LUTs lead in 22/24 cells; the largest index holds 17.78 million vectors at 20.44\,GiB resident memory. Full-pool calibration meets a $10^{-3}$ held-out
recall-loss target relative to the best tested budget in 12/12 cells, with
maximum loss 0.0006; smaller samples expose workload-dependent quality risk.
At recall 0.97 and batch 1,000, JHQ leads in three of four datasets and is
near parity with IVF-RaBitQ on arXiv. OpenAI runs use TF32; FP32 checks
retain favourable comparisons under a TF32-trained cache. At batch 8 and
the same recall, CAGRA fp32 leads on all four datasets. These results
locate the execution, quality and capacity trade-offs of GPU JHQ.
changes.after:
\frontchapter{Abstract}
Approximate nearest-neighbour (ANN) search supports similarity retrieval
over large collections of embedding vectors. GPUs accelerate this search,
but limited device memory makes compressed indexes attractive. JHQ is a
hierarchical quantisation method that screens candidates with compact
codes and refines a smaller set using residual codes. This thesis develops
JHQ-GPU to study how this representation can support efficient GPU
construction and search.

The implementation combines GPU model fitting and batched encoding with
bounded input staging and a packed, list-ordered layout. Its scan replaces
each 256-entry distance table with two 16-entry tables, preserving scores
in real arithmetic. Grouped scanning preserves exact global candidate
selection under a fixed ordering of computed scores and positions. Calibration chooses how
many candidates to refine without ground-truth labels, by comparing
returned neighbours with a larger-budget reference.

Evaluation on an NVIDIA RTX~5090 compares methods on Vogue, arXiv,
OpenAI-1536 and OpenAI-3072. At recall 0.97 and batch 1,000, JHQ-GPU
delivers $1.32$--$1.75\times$ the host-to-host throughput of CAGRA fp32
across all four datasets and is the fastest tested method on three.
For the larger BGE and Stella datasets, whose raw FP32 vectors exceed
device memory, JHQ-GPU enables single-GPU search; the largest index
contains 17.78 million vectors and uses 20.44\,GiB of resident GPU memory.

\frontchapter{摘要}
近似最近邻（ANN）搜索支持大规模嵌入向量集合上的相似性检索。GPU 可以加速搜索，但有限显存使压缩索引具有吸引力。JHQ 是一种层级量化方法：先用紧凑编码筛选候选，再利用残差编码对较小的候选集精排。本文开发 JHQ-GPU，研究如何利用这种表示实现高效的 GPU 建库与搜索。

实现将 GPU 模型拟合和分批编码，与有界输入暂存、打包且按倒排列表排列的布局结合。扫描将每张 256 项距离表替换为两张 16 项表，保持实数算术下的分数。分组扫描在固定的已计算分数与位置排序下，保持精确的全局候选选择。校准通过比较当前结果与较大预算参考返回的近邻，在无需真值标签的情况下决定精排候选数量。

在 NVIDIA RTX~5090 上，跨方法评测使用 Vogue、arXiv、OpenAI-1536 和 OpenAI-3072。在召回率 0.97、batch 1,000 下，JHQ-GPU 在这四个数据集上的主机到主机吞吐为 CAGRA fp32 的 $1.32$--$1.75\times$，并在其中三个数据集上取得已测方法的最高吞吐。对于更大规模的 BGE 和 Stella，原始 FP32 向量的存储需求已超出设备显存，JHQ-GPU 仍可在单张 GPU 上完成搜索；最大索引包含 17.78 百万个向量，常驻 GPU 显存为 20.44\,GiB。

Define hardware, tested settings, host-to-host timing and interpolated recall comparison.
Use the four E1 CAGRA fp32 ratios 1.416,1.317,1.747,1.747 to report rounded 1.32–1.75.

Do not claim one-third memory because net-process and index allocations have different boundaries.
